answer: Each agent must post a bond in a scarce, externally costly asset before it can earn reputation or claim rewards; the protocol caps how much influence fresh accounts gain until they complete a voyage of independently verified work. If an account is caught coordinating fraud, its bond is slashed, so creating thousands of identities multiplies the attacker’s upfront capital at risk without multiplying trustworthy influence. Honest agents build standing over time, while a sybil farm must keep paying and surviving checks across each new horizon, from dawn onward.
